stories.title: GPR41 deficiency worsens experimental colitis and accompanies gut microbiota changes
stories.takeaway: Loss of the short-chain fatty-acid receptor GPR41 exacerbated DSS-induced colitis in an experimental model.
stories.what_happened: Tomikawa and colleagues investigated GPR41 deficiency during dextran sulfate sodium-induced colitis and reported more severe disease alongside altered gut microbial composition.
stories.why_it_matters: Adds mechanistic context to research on microbial metabolites, host sensing and intestinal inflammation.
stories.caveat: An experimental colitis model does not establish a therapeutic effect of GPR41 targeting in human IBD; microbial changes are associations.

stories.title: UniMAG assembles a cross-habitat catalogue of more than 581,000 microbial genomes
stories.takeaway: A new metagenomic reference integrates 581,345 quality-controlled genomes, including 342,875 from human gut samples.
stories.what_happened: Gautam and Marsh compiled published and publicly deposited metagenome-assembled genomes from human gut, animal gut and environmental sources into UniMAG v1.0.
stories.why_it_matters: A larger harmonized genome reference may help microbial taxonomy and comparative metagenomic analysis.
stories.caveat: Catalogue coverage reflects existing sampling and assembly biases; genome recovery does not demonstrate expression or function.

stories.title: Clostridial Delta toxin implicated in intestinal and brain injury in necrotizing enterocolitis
stories.takeaway: A research highlight describes experimental evidence linking Clostridium perfringens Delta toxin to multiorgan NEC-like injury.
stories.what_happened: A Nature Reviews Microbiology highlight discusses Zhang and colleagues' genomic, organoid and animal work comparing toxin-positive and toxin-negative strains and testing purified toxin.
stories.why_it_matters: Points to a potentially important microbial virulence mechanism in neonatal intestinal disease.
stories.caveat: This is a commentary on another study; animal and organoid evidence does not establish that the toxin explains all clinical NEC cases.

stories.title: Candidalysin review examines fungal commensalism, epithelial injury and mucosal immunity
stories.takeaway: A decade-spanning review synthesizes how a Candida albicans peptide toxin participates in infection and host responses, including gut commensalism.
stories.what_happened: Richardson and colleagues review candidalysin as a virulence and commensal-associated factor, its epithelial immune signaling, and outstanding therapeutic questions.
stories.why_it_matters: Expands host–microbiome thinking beyond bacteria to fungal molecules and context-dependent epithelial responses.
stories.caveat: Review synthesis rather than a new experimental validation; mechanisms and consequences vary by tissue and disease model.

stories.title: Antimicrobial white light assessed in primary human cells and three-dimensional skin models
stories.takeaway: An experimental study reports antimicrobial illumination conditions without detectable cytotoxic or genotoxic injury in the tested skin models.
stories.what_happened: Bartolocci and colleagues evaluated broad-spectrum white light in primary keratinocytes, dermal fibroblasts and 3D human skin models to assess tissue homeostasis and photobiological safety.
stories.why_it_matters: Illustrates why antimicrobial technologies should be assessed alongside human-relevant tissue viability and damage endpoints.
stories.caveat: Results depend on illumination conditions and tested models; lack of detectable injury is not proof of universal clinical safety.
